headys_lumen.config.title: Heady's Lumen: ShaderLights
headys_lumen.config.enabled.tooltip: Master switch. When off, the mod does nothing.
headys_lumen.config.match_suffix.tooltip: Any modded item whose id ends in "torch" (e.g. somemod:lantern_torch) lights up in shaders. Vanilla items are left to the shader pack unless you add them to your Light items list.
headys_lumen.config.light_level.tooltip: Light level (1-15) given to auto-detected items.
headys_lumen.config.spoof_id: Pretend to be a normal torch
headys_lumen.config.spoof_id.tooltip: Tells the shader pack the item is minecraft:torch when nothing better applies, so you get the pack's torch light. Skipped if the pack already knows the item.
headys_lumen.config.send_color.tooltip: Passes each item's colour to Iris' heldBlockLightColor value. Shader packs that read it show your exact colour. Needs "colored lighting" in the pack to be on.
headys_lumen.config.nearest_item: Match closest item (packs without colour support)
headys_lumen.config.nearest_item.tooltip: For packs that colour handheld light per item: the shader is told the item is whichever item the pack knows with the closest colour. Use "Pretend to be" on an item to choose it yourself.
headys_lumen.config.items.tooltip: Press + to add an item. Press X on a row to remove it.
headys_lumen.config.items.help: Press + to add a row. Each row is one item: its ID, how bright it is, what colour, and optionally which item the shader should think it is.
headys_lumen.config.item.id.tooltip: e.g. examplemod:blue_torch. Vanilla items work too: add minecraft:torch with a colour to recolour torches. You can use * as a wildcard (examplemod:*_lamp). /lumen addheld adds the item in your hand.
headys_lumen.config.item.intensity.toolt: Held light level 1-15, used exactly: it can also dim an item that already glows by itself. 0 = no held light at all, for items such as unlit or burnt-out torches (e.g. *:unlit_torch). Heady's Lumen: ShaderPack_PhotonFork uses it for brightness AND reach. Photon, Solas and Rethinking Voxels ignore it; in Rethinking Voxels the mod dims the colour instead.
headys_lumen.config.item.use_color.toolt: Off = the shader pack picks the colour. On = use the Hue and Saturation sliders below.
headys_lumen.config.item.hue.tooltip: Slide to pick the colour. The label and the Preview box show what you are picking.
headys_lumen.config.item.saturation.tool: 0 = white light, 100 = fully coloured. The Preview box shows hue + saturation + intensity together.
headys_lumen.config.item.pretend.tooltip: For shader packs that colour held lights per item. Pick an item the pack knows (e.g. minecraft:sea_lantern for a cyan glow). Empty = automatic. Type any item id or choose from the list.
headys_lumen.config.invalid_id: Invalid item id. Use modid:item (lowercase letters, digits, _ . - / and * wildcards).
headys_lumen.config.missing_cloth.1: The in-game editor needs Cloth Config.
headys_lumen.config.missing_cloth.2: Install it, or edit config/lumen.json and use /lumen reload.
headys_lumen.config.rgb_id_mode.tooltip: Rethinking Voxels reads the item id as a colour, so the mod can send your EXACT colour (16 steps per channel) by choosing the id. Auto-detect checks the pack's ids for torch / soul torch / redstone torch. Use 'Always on' if detection misses your pack.
